source.title: Benign Overfitting without Linearity: Neural Network Classifiers Trained by Gradient Descent for Noisy Linear Data
source.authors: Spencer Frei; Niladri S. Chatterji; P. Bartlett

record.tranche_reason: The paper theoretically analyzes gradient-descent fitting and generalization under label noise, using synthetic high-dimensional mixture data rather than reproducing the original image experiments.
record.gate_note: The theorem reports interpolation and a test-error bound for noisy labels. Results cited from prior studies are not included as rows. The iteration bound and weight movement do not compare training time across noise rates or test the listed versions independently.
record.test_reason: The paper proves interpolation of partly corrupted training labels in a synthetic mixture model, bearing on V4. Its proof also establishes that clean and noisy training labels are all classified correctly after one gradient step, bearing on V6's proposed learning order.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is substantially accurate: under the stated mixture, dimension, separation, noise, initialization, and step-size assumptions, finite-width two-layer networks trained by unregularized gradient descent interpolate noisy labels and have test error bounded by η plus an exponential term. Minimax optimality up to constants in the exponent is established for random classification noise, rather than arbitrary adversarial corruption.
record.recipe_differences: Theoretical analysis of full-batch gradient descent on a synthetic noisy mixture with smoothed leaky ReLU networks; the original studies are empirical investigations of deep-network generalization on image datasets.
record.method_sensitivity: The guarantee depends on the high-dimensional and class-separation assumptions, bounded noise rate η ≤ 1/C, and the stated step-size and initialization conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: The noisy-distribution test-error bound establishes benign overfitting under high-dimensional mixture assumptions, but does not measure a monotonic degradation curve.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Two-layer networks can interpolate bounded label corruption while retaining low error on the underlying clean classification problem.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Conference on Computational Learning Theory (COLT), 2022
record.problems: The evidence is a theoretical guarantee for a restricted synthetic data model, bounded noise rates, and stated parameter assumptions; no empirical evaluation or noise-rate sweep is reported.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results in the paper directly test the listed versions. Cited prior-work results, the training-iteration bound without a clean-versus-noisy comparison, and the weight-distance proposition were not extracted as rows.

untested.parts: Completely random labeling, chance test performance, and fitting with unchanged standard training hyperparameters.
Relative training time for true versus random labels and slowing convergence as corruption increases. The iteration bound supplies neither comparison.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or unstructured Gaussian-noise inputs. Gaussian mixture clusters retain class signal.
Corruption beyond η ≤ 1/C, including fully random labels, and steady degradation of clean-label test performance toward chance.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting, and the consequences of removing them for true-label generalization.
Relative clean-versus-noisy loss convergence times and learning order outside the specified high-dimensional, small-initialization regime.

missing.what: Add the guarantee that all training points, including corrupted-label points, are classified correctly after one gradient step and remain correctly classified. Record its theoretical nature and assumptions A1–A6. The bounded sigmoid-loss ratios provide context but do not independently establish identical learning times.
missing.locator: Lemma A.3(c), pp. 23–26; proof of Lemma 4.8, equation (22), p. 27

record.verdict_notes: Restricted assumptions and untested corruption rates do not themselves justify limits_scope. R2's upper bound cannot establish either partial or absent monotonic degradation. The V6 qualification concerns classification at discrete iterations, not equality of clean and noisy loss trajectories.

versions.untested_parts: Completely random labels, chance test error, and fitting under the original image settings are not tested; the paper assumes noise rate η ≤ 1/C.
No comparison of training time for clean versus random labels or of convergence time across corruption fractions.
No shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
The paper does not sweep corruption from none to all or report a steady rise toward chance; its guarantee is for η ≤ 1/C and does not report empirical results.
Weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation are not tested.
The paper does not compare learning order for clean versus noisy labels over training.

rows.measure: Empirical training loss and training classification error
rows.value: L̂(W⁽ᵀ⁾) ≤ ε; all training points classified correctly
rows.uncertainty: With probability at least 1 − 2δ over random initialization and sample draws
rows.note: The guarantee covers noisy training labels in the stated synthetic distribution and bounded noise-rate regime; it does not establish fitting fully random labels.
rows.check: The interpolation guarantee is correct under assumptions A1–A6. Specify smoothed leaky activations, fixed random output weights, and constrained initialization and step size. This establishes perfect fitting only for the bounded-noise portion of V4.

conditions.value: high-dimensional mixture of well-separated class-conditional strongly log-concave distributions
n∥µ∥⁴ ≫ p for test error close to η

rows.uncertainty: With probability at least 1 − 2δ over random initialization and sample draws
rows.note: A theoretical upper bound close to the noise rate is given in the stated regime; there is no reported sweep showing a steady increase in test error toward chance.
rows.check: An upper bound of η + 2 exp(−n∥µ∥⁴/(Cp)) does not establish that actual test error increases steadily with corruption. Test error is evaluated against labels from the noisy distribution P; η bounds its label-flip probability and is not necessarily the actual noise rate for arbitrary adversarial corruption. This differs from evaluating against clean test labels.
